language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

<meta>The OCR flagged that the Mongolian body text and the Mongolian margin label could not be read reliably. They are reproduced below as unread regions. Only the Chinese margin label has been translated.</meta>

<margin><unclear>short Mongolian margin label in the left margin (title/volume/folio), not transcribed</unclear></margin>

<unclear>approximately 30 columns of Classical Mongolian woodblock text (Uighur-Mongol script), read left to right, not transcribed</unclear>

<margin>Various Perfection of Wisdom Sutras, Volume One, upper side, 193 <note>original: "諸般般若經第一卷上一百九十三". "Various Perfection of Wisdom Sutras" is the Chinese name for the miscellaneous Prajñāpāramitā section of the Kanjur, the Buddhist canon. The character 上, "upper," most likely marks the front side of the leaf. 193 is the folio number.</note></margin>

<note>A rectangle with a double-ruled border surrounds the block of text. Narrow ruled panels on either side hold the margin labels.</note>

<summary>Folio 193 of the first volume of the Kanjur section of miscellaneous Perfection of Wisdom sutras, printed from woodblocks in Classical Mongolian with red ink. The Mongolian text was not transcribed, so only the Chinese margin label, which gives the section, volume and folio number, can be translated.</summary>
